title: Detecting Sycophancy Without Ground Truth: Consistency-Based Self-Evaluation

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Downgraded. ELEPHANT and multi-turn consistency methods already provide ground-truth-free sycophancy detection. The proposed approach adds marginal value over existing published methods.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running each question twice (neutral, pressured) and comparing answers is simple. Flagging differences requires basic string comparison or LLM judge. Pure API work, trivially accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Clear experiment: run questions in two conditions, measure consistency, validate against gold labels. Single deliverable: consistency-based sycophancy measure with validation statistics. Achievable in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: ELEPHANT (arXiv:2505.13995, 2025) directly addresses sycophancy measurement without ground truth by defining social sycophancy as excessive face preservation and using a symmetry test: if an LLM affirms both sides of a conflict when presented to different users, it is sycophantic regardless of ground truth. SycEval (arXiv:2502.08177, 2025) measures sycophancy across domains including medicine where ground truth is ambiguous. 'Measuring Sycophancy of Language Models in Multi-turn Conversations' (EMNLP Findings 2025) uses consistency scores across multi-turn interactions. The proposed neutral-vs-pressured dual-query approach is a specific variant of consistency-based detection, but the core methodology — detecting sycophancy via consistency without ground truth — is well-established in 2025 literature.
